XTEND Expands XOS-Powered Robotics Ecosystem into Ground Domain with AtlasROVER

children: First AtlasROVER deployment since XTEND’s acquisition of Atlas extends XOS-powered systems from air into ground robotics

announced today that XTEND, a leader in AI-powered robotics and developer of XOS, the operating system for Physical AI, today announced the first deployment of an XOS-powered AtlasROVER to a customer in the Asia-Pacific region since XTEND’s acquisition of Atlas.

The deployment marks an important step in demonstrating XTEND’s strategy to extend XOS beyond aerial systems into ground robotics, building toward a common software layer across air, ground and ultimately maritime robotic systems.

XOS is XTEND’s hardware-agnostic operating system for human-guided autonomy, designed to bring common AI capabilities, mission applications and operator workflows across different robotic platforms. Integrating AtlasROVER into the XOS ecosystem expands that software architecture into the ground domain.

“This is an important step in demonstrating the strategy behind XOS,” said Aviv Shapira, CEO and co-founder of XTEND. “Our goal is not to build isolated robotic products, but to create a common software layer that can extend across air, ground and ultimately maritime systems. Bringing AtlasROVER into the XOS ecosystem moves us closer to a future where different robotic platforms can work together, while humans remain in control of the decisions that matter.”

AtlasROVER is a ground robotic platform designed to operate in complex environments and support multiple mission payloads. Its integration with XOS expands the range of robotic platforms within XTEND’s software ecosystem and demonstrates how the company is extending its software-first approach across multiple physical domains.

XTEND is a leader in software systems and Physical AI, deployed in high-threat, complex operational environments where human exposure carries significant risk. Powered by its proprietary XTEND Operating System (XOS), XTEND’s integrated software and advanced robotic hardware solutions are designed to provide autonomy at the edge. Operating across Defense, Homeland Security, and Commercial Security missions through a platform of robots, drones, and robotic subsystems, XTEND’s open architecture platform facilitates scalability across partners and third-party applications. With over 12,500 systems deployed in over 30 countries, XTEND’s solutions have been validated in five combat zones and operationally deployed by national defense, special-mission units, and security organizations across the globe. Founded in Tel Aviv, Israel, and headquartered in Tampa, Florida, XTEND delivers NDAA-compliant solutions through a global network of regional XFAB manufacturing facilities located in the U.S., the U.K., Singapore, Israel, and Latvia.
